records.source: שִׁמְע֞וּ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עַ֚ל כָּל־הַמִּשְׁפָּחָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֶעֱלֵ֛יתִי מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: Hear this word which Yahweh has spoken against you, sons of Israel, against the whole clan which I brought up from [the] land of Egypt, saying:
pieces: Hear this word that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken against you, {{gender:people|sons}} of Israel, \q against the whole family \q that I brought up from the land of Egypt:

L.1: Hear this word that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken against you, {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, \q against the whole clan \q that I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying:

R.1: People of Israel, listen to this message that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken against you, \q against the whole family \q that I brought out of the land of Egypt:

decisions.choice: the LORD has spoken ... that I brought up: the prophet's call to listen runs straight into the LORD's own words
decisions.reason: The verse begins with the prophet speaking of the LORD as "he" and ends with the LORD saying "I". Amos often moves between the two voices without a break; the message is the LORD's either way.

decisions.choice: the whole clan: all Israel, the whole people the LORD brought out of Egypt
decisions.reason: The word means a clan or extended family. Here it covers the whole people that came out of Egypt, Judah as well as the northern kingdom, spoken of as one family. Verse 2 uses the same word for "all the clans of the earth".

decisions.choice: clan (L), family (B, R); saying (L only)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "family", to match "all the families of the earth" in verse 2 at those levels. The Hebrew ends with "saying", which Literal keeps; the other levels let the colon do its work.

records.heading: You alone have I known

records.source: רַ֚ק אֶתְכֶ֣ם יָדַ֔עְתִּי מִכֹּ֖ל מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת הָאֲדָמָ֑ה עַל־כֵּן֙ אֶפְקֹ֣ד עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת כָּל־עֲוֺנֹֽתֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Only you I have known from all [the] clans of the earth; therefore I will visit on you all your iniquities.
pieces: You alone have I known \q out of all the families of the earth; \q that is why I will punish you \q for all your sins.

L.2: Only you have I known \q of all the clans of the earth; \q therefore I will visit on you \q all your iniquities.

R.2: I chose only you to be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own \q out of all the families on earth. \q That is why I will punish you \q for all your sins.

decisions.choice: only you have I known: the LORD chose Israel and bound himself to it
decisions.reason: "Know" here is the knowing of a close, chosen relationship, not knowledge of facts: the LORD "knew" Abraham, choosing him (Genesis 18:19), and "knew" Israel in the wilderness, caring for it (Hosea 13:5; compare Jeremiah 1:5). The LORD knows all nations, as chapters 1-2 show, but only Israel is his own.

decisions.choice: all the clans of the earth: the words of the promise to Abraham
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one used when God promised that "all the families of the earth" would be blessed through Abraham (Genesis 12:3; 28:14). Israel was chosen from among them.

decisions.choice: therefore I will punish you: being chosen makes Israel more accountable, not safe
decisions.reason: Amos's hearers would expect "therefore I will protect you". The LORD says the opposite: because he chose Israel, he will hold it to account for every wrong. The verb, often translated "visit", means to attend to someone, here to punish (Exodus 32:34; Hosea 1:4); it returns twice in verse 14.

decisions.choice: known (L, B), chose ... to be my own (R); iniquities (L), sins (B, R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "known" means here (m1). "Iniquities" and "sins" follow the settled wording for this word.

records.gloss: Do walk two together unless they have met by appointment?
pieces: Do two people walk together \q unless they have agreed to meet?

L.3: Do two walk together \q unless they have met by appointment?

R.3: Do two people travel together \q unless they have planned to meet?

decisions.choice: a chain of questions (verses 3-8), each expecting "No": nothing happens without a cause
decisions.reason: Verses 3-6 ask seven questions, each describing an effect that does not happen without its cause: two travelers meet because they arranged it; a lion roars because it has prey; a trap springs because something is caught; a city trembles because the alarm is sounded; disaster strikes because the LORD sends it. The questions start with harmless pictures and grow more frightening. Verse 8 draws the conclusion: the prophet speaks because the LORD has spoken. It is Amos's answer to those who tell him to be silent (2:12; 7:12-13).

decisions.choice: met by appointment: arranged to meet at a set time and place
decisions.reason: The verb means to meet by agreement, at an appointed place (Exodus 25:22; Joshua 11:5). The Septuagint reads "unless they know each other". Some readers see in the two the LORD and his prophet, or the LORD and Israel, but the question is first of all a picture from daily life.

decisions.choice: two people (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "two"; Balanced and Readable add "people" for clear English.

records.source: הֲיִשְׁאַ֤ג אַרְיֵה֙ בַּיַּ֔עַר וְטֶ֖רֶף אֵ֣ין ל֑וֹ הֲיִתֵּ֨ן כְּפִ֤יר קוֹלוֹ֙ מִמְּעֹ֣נָת֔וֹ בִּלְתִּ֖י אִם־לָכָֽד׃
records.gloss: Does roar a lion in the forest when prey there is not for it? Does give a young lion its voice from its den unless it has caught [something]?
pieces: Does a lion roar in the forest \q when it has no prey? \q Does a young lion growl from its den \q unless it has caught something?

L.4: Does a lion roar in the forest \q when it has no prey? \q Does a young lion utter its voice from its den \q unless it has caught [something]?

R.4: Does a lion roar in the forest \q if it has not found an animal to eat? \q Does a young lion growl in its den \q if it has not caught anything?

decisions.choice: the lion's roar: the picture of 1:2, where the LORD roars from Zion
decisions.reason: A lion roars over prey it has already taken, and growls in its den over what it has caught. The image recalls 1:2 and points ahead to verse 8: if the LORD has roared, his judgment is already certain.

decisions.choice: a young lion: a lion old enough to hunt for itself
decisions.reason: The word is used of a lion in its full strength, hunting its own prey (Ezekiel 19:3; Judges 14:5).

decisions.choice: utter its voice (L), growl (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the phrase used of the LORD in 1:2 ("utters his voice"), so the reader can see the link; Balanced and Readable say what a lion does.

records.source: הֲתִפֹּ֤ל צִפּוֹר֙ עַל־פַּ֣ח הָאָ֔רֶץ וּמוֹקֵ֖שׁ אֵ֣ין לָ֑הּ הֲיַֽעֲלֶה־פַּח֙ מִן־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה וְלָכ֖וֹד לֹ֥א יִלְכּֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: Does fall a bird into a trap of the ground when a snare there is not for it? Does spring up a trap from the ground and surely catch not it catches?
pieces: Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground \q if no snare has been set for it? \q Does a trap spring up from the ground \q when it has caught nothing?

L.5: Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground \q when there is no snare for it? \q Does a trap spring up from the ground \q when it has caught nothing at all?

R.5: Does a bird get caught in a trap on the ground \q if no one has set a trap for it? \q Does a trap spring shut \q if it has caught nothing?

decisions.choice: trap ... snare: two words for a bird trap
decisions.reason: The first word is a net or clap-trap; the second may be the snare itself, its trigger, or the bait. The point is plain: a bird is not caught unless a trap has been set.

decisions.choice: a trap that springs up from the ground: a net that snaps shut when the bird touches it
decisions.reason: A fowler's trap lay on the ground and sprang up and closed when a bird touched the trigger. It does not spring unless something has set it off. Amos's hearers would know such traps well, and the picture is a hint that Israel is already caught.

records.source: אִם־יִתָּקַ֤ע שׁוֹפָר֙ בְּעִ֔יר וְעָ֖ם לֹ֣א יֶחֱרָ֑דוּ אִם־תִּהְיֶ֤ה רָעָה֙ בְּעִ֔יר וַיהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א עָשָֽׂה׃
records.gloss: Or is blown a trumpet in a city and [the] people not tremble? Or is there calamity in a city and Yahweh not has done [it]?
pieces: If a ram's horn is blown in a city, \q do the people not tremble? \q If disaster comes to a city, \q has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} not done it?

L.6: Is a trumpet blown in a city \q and the people do not tremble? \q Is there calamity in a city \q and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has not done [it]?

R.6: When a warning trumpet sounds in a city, \q are the people not afraid? \q When disaster comes to a city, \q is it not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who sent it?

decisions.choice: a trumpet blown in a city: the watchman's alarm that an enemy is coming
decisions.reason: A watchman blew the ram's horn to warn a city of attack (Jeremiah 6:1, 17; Ezekiel 33:3-6; Hosea 5:8). When it sounds, everyone trembles. Amos's words are such an alarm.

decisions.choice: calamity in a city that the LORD has not done: the disaster coming on Israel is the LORD's doing
decisions.reason: "Calamity" here is disaster, not moral evil, as in Isaiah 45:7. The question expects the answer that the LORD is behind it. Amos does not offer a general teaching about every misfortune; he insists that what is about to strike Israel, like the disasters of 4:6-11, comes from the LORD, and so it has a reason and calls for a response.

decisions.choice: trumpet (L, R), ram's horn (B); calamity (L), disaster (B, R)
decisions.reason: The ram's horn follows the settled wording: "trumpet" at Literal and Readable and "ram's horn" at Balanced. Readable adds "warning" to say what it was blown for (m1).

records.source: כִּ֣י לֹ֧א יַעֲשֶׂ֛ה אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה דָּבָ֑ר כִּ֚י אִם־גָּלָ֣ה סוֹד֔וֹ אֶל־עֲבָדָ֖יו הַנְּבִיאִֽים׃
records.gloss: For not does [the] Lord Yahweh a thing unless he has revealed his secret to his servants the prophets.
pieces: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} does nothing at all \q unless {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} first reveals {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} plan \q to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the prophets.

L.7: For the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} does not do a thing \q unless {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has revealed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} secret \q to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the prophets.

R.7: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} does nothing \q without first telling {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} plans \q to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the prophets.

decisions.choice: a statement in the middle of the questions, giving the reason for them
decisions.reason: Verse 7 breaks the chain of questions with a plain statement. It explains how the questions apply to Amos: the LORD does not act without first telling his prophets, so when a prophet speaks, it is because the LORD is about to act. Verse 8 then gives the last two questions.

decisions.choice: his secret: his plan, shared in his council
decisions.reason: The word means a confidential talk, a council, or the plan made there. The true prophet is one who has "stood in the council of the LORD" and heard his word (Jeremiah 23:18, 22).

decisions.choice: his servants the prophets: the standing title for the LORD's prophets
decisions.reason: The phrase is used often of the prophets the LORD sent to warn Israel (2 Kings 17:13, 23; Jeremiah 7:25). "Servant" here is a title of honor: one who acts for the LORD.

decisions.choice: secret (L), plan (B), plans (R); servants (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: "Servants" is kept at every level, as in the published "my servants the prophets" (Jeremiah 7:25; 2 Kings 17:13): the phrase is a title, and "slaves" would mislead. Balanced and Readable say "plan" for "secret" (m2).

records.source: אַרְיֵ֥ה שָׁאָ֖ג מִ֣י לֹ֣א יִירָ֑א אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ דִּבֶּ֔ר מִ֖י לֹ֥א יִנָּבֵֽא׃
records.gloss: A lion has roared; who will not fear? [The] Lord Yahweh has spoken; who will not prophesy?
pieces: The lion has roared; who will not be afraid? \q The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} has spoken; \q who can keep from prophesying?

L.8: A lion has roared; who would not fear? \q The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} has spoken; \q who would not prophesy?

R.8: The lion has roared. Who would not be afraid? \q The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} has spoken. \q Who could keep from prophesying?

decisions.choice: the end of the chain: the lion is the LORD, and his roar compels
decisions.reason: The lion of verse 4 returns, and now it is plain who the lion is: the LORD who roars from Zion (1:2). As a lion's roar fills everyone with fear, the LORD's word leaves the prophet no choice. Amos did not set himself up as a prophet; the LORD took him and sent him (7:14-15; compare Jeremiah 20:9).

decisions.choice: who will not prophesy?: who could keep from prophesying?
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no one". It speaks first of the prophet, who must speak when the LORD has spoken; it also hints that all who hear should take up the warning.

decisions.choice: who will not prophesy (L), who can keep from prophesying (B, R); The lion (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the question means (m2). They say "The lion" because the lion of verse 4 is meant.

records.source: הַשְׁמִ֨יעוּ֙ עַל־אַרְמְנ֣וֹת בְּאַשְׁדּ֔וֹד וְעַֽל־אַרְמְנ֖וֹת בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְאִמְר֗וּ הֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ עַל־הָרֵ֣י שֹׁמְר֔וֹן וּרְא֞וּ מְהוּמֹ֤ת רַבּוֹת֙ בְּתוֹכָ֔הּ וַעֲשׁוּקִ֖ים בְּקִרְבָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Proclaim to [the] fortresses in Ashdod and to [the] fortresses in [the] land of Egypt, and say: Gather yourselves on [the] mountains of Samaria, and see [the] great tumults within her and [the] oppressions in her midst.
pieces: Announce to the fortresses of Ashdod \q and to the fortresses in the land of Egypt, and say: \q "Assemble on the mountains around Samaria \q and see the great turmoil within her \q and the oppression in her midst."

L.9: Proclaim to the fortresses in Ashdod \q and to the fortresses in the land of Egypt, \q and say, "Gather on the mountains of Samaria, \q and see the great tumults within her \q and the oppressions in her midst."

R.9: Announce this to the fortresses of Ashdod \q and to the fortresses of Egypt. Tell them: \q "Come to the hills around Samaria. \q See the great disorder in that city \q and how its people are oppressed."

decisions.choice: Ashdod and Egypt called as witnesses against Samaria
decisions.reason: The LORD summons foreign peoples, the Philistines and Egypt, Israel's old oppressors, to come and look at what goes on in Samaria. Even they will be shocked. Their testimony is what verse 13 calls for.

decisions.choice: Ashdod: the Philistine city, as the Hebrew reads
decisions.reason: The Septuagint reads "Assyria" here, which would pair the two great powers, Assyria and Egypt, as Hosea does (Hosea 7:11; 9:3). The Hebrew reads Ashdod, one of the Philistine cities of 1:8, and is followed here.

decisions.choice: the mountains of Samaria: the hills around the capital
decisions.reason: Samaria, the capital of the northern kingdom, was built by Omri on a hill (1 Kings 16:24), with higher hills around it. From them the witnesses could look down into the city.

decisions.choice: tumults ... oppressions: disorder in the city and the wrongs done to the weak
decisions.reason: The first word means confusion and unrest, the turmoil of a city where might is right. The second means acts of oppression, or the oppressed themselves.

decisions.choice: the hills around Samaria; how its people are oppressed
decisions.reason: Readable says "around", as the witnesses look into the city from the hills (m3), and puts "oppressions" as a clause.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־יָדְע֥וּ עֲשׂוֹת־נְכֹחָ֖ה נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה הָאֽוֹצְרִ֛ים חָמָ֥ס וָשֹׁ֖ד בְּאַרְמְנֽוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And not they know to do right, declares Yahweh, those who store up violence and devastation in their fortresses.
pieces: They do not know how to do right, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q these people who hoard violence and destruction in their fortresses.

L.10: And they do not know how to do what is right, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q those who store up violence and destruction in their fortresses.

R.10: They do not even know how to do what is right, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q They fill their fortresses with things they took by violence and robbery.

decisions.choice: what is right: what is straight and honest
decisions.reason: The word means what is straight, upright, honest (Isaiah 26:10; 59:14). They have done wrong so long that they no longer know how to do right.

decisions.choice: store up violence and destruction: fill their houses with what they took by violence
decisions.reason: "Violence and destruction" stands for what violence and robbery bring in. Their fortresses are stocked with stolen goods; what they treasure is the fruit of crime. The same pair of words is in Jeremiah 6:7 and Ezekiel 45:9.

decisions.choice: things they took by violence and robbery
decisions.reason: Readable says what is stored (m2).

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה צַ֖ר וּסְבִ֣יב הָאָ֑רֶץ וְהוֹרִ֤ד מִמֵּךְ֙ עֻזֵּ֔ךְ וְנָבֹ֖זּוּ אַרְמְנוֹתָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: An enemy, and around the land! And he will bring down from you your strength, and will be plundered your fortresses.
pieces: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: \q An enemy will surround the land; \q he will tear down your strongholds, \q and your fortresses will be plundered.

L.11: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: \q An enemy, and all around the land! \q He will bring down your strength from you, \q and your fortresses will be plundered.

R.11: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: \q An enemy will surround your land. \q He will tear down your defenses \q and rob your fortresses.

decisions.choice: An enemy, and all around the land!: an enemy will surround the land
alternatives: an enemy will surround the land
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is abrupt, like a cry of alarm: "An enemy, and around the land!". It means that an enemy will be on every side. Some ancient translations and many scholars read the letters of "around" as a verb, "will surround"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: an enemy: not named, but Assyria took Samaria in 722 BC
decisions.reason: Amos never names the enemy. Within about forty years Assyria besieged Samaria for three years and took it, and carried its people into exile (2 Kings 17:5-6).

decisions.choice: your strength: your strongholds and defenses
decisions.reason: The word means strength and also what gives strength: walls, towers, and the fortresses where they kept their wealth.

decisions.choice: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD (L), Therefore the Lord GOD says this (B), So this is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula follows the settled wording for "thus says", with "therefore" before it.

records.heading: An enemy will surround the land

records.source: כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ יַצִּ֨יל הָרֹעֶ֜ה מִפִּ֧י הָאֲרִ֛י שְׁתֵּ֥י כְרָעַ֖יִם א֣וֹ בְדַל־אֹ֑זֶן כֵּ֣ן יִנָּצְל֞וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן בִּפְאַ֥ת מִטָּ֖ה וּבִדְמֶ֥שֶׁק עָֽרֶשׂ׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh: As rescues the shepherd from [the] mouth of the lion two legs or a piece of an ear, so will be rescued [the] sons of Israel, those who dwell in Samaria, with [the] corner of a bed and with [the] silk of a couch.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: \q As a shepherd snatches from a lion's mouth just two legs or a scrap of an ear, \q so will the {{gender:people|sons}} of Israel who live in Samaria be rescued, \q with nothing but the corner of a bed or a scrap of silk from a couch.

L.12: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q As the shepherd rescues from the mouth of the lion two legs or the tip of an ear, \q so will the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel be rescued, who dwell in Samaria, \q with the corner of a bed and with the silk of a couch.

R.12: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q A shepherd may save only two legs or a piece of an ear from a lion's mouth. \q That is how the people of Israel who live in Samaria will be rescued. \q All that will be left is the corner of a bed or a scrap of silk from a couch.

decisions.choice: a shepherd rescues two legs or a piece of an ear: the remains that prove the sheep is dead
decisions.reason: A shepherd who lost a sheep to a wild animal brought back what was left of it as proof that it had been killed, not stolen, so that he would not have to pay for it (Exodus 22:12; Genesis 31:39). So the "rescue" of Israel is no rescue at all: what is left only proves that the nation has been destroyed.

decisions.choice: with the corner of a bed and with the silk of a couch: all that is left of Samaria's rich is a scrap of their fine furniture
alternatives: those who sit in Samaria on the corner of a bed and on the silk cushions of a couch
a piece of the leg of a couch
decisions.reason: The last line is hard. Read with the picture of the shepherd, it lists what will be "rescued": a corner of a bed and a scrap of a couch, as useless as two legs and an ear. It can also be read with "who dwell in Samaria", describing the rich who sit at ease on the corners of their beds and couches (compare 6:4). The word translated "silk" is not found elsewhere; it looks like the name Damascus, and has been taken as a fine cloth, as "in Damascus", or as part of a couch, such as its leg.

decisions.choice: a bed ... a couch: the luxury furniture of the rich
decisions.reason: Beds and couches for reclining at meals, some inlaid with ivory, were signs of wealth (6:4). The rich of Samaria will lose everything but a scrap of them.

decisions.choice: just, nothing but (B); All that will be left (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the irony plain: only scraps are rescued (m1, m2).

records.source: שִׁמְע֥וּ וְהָעִ֖ידוּ בְּבֵ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב נְאֻם־אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י הַצְּבָאֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Hear and testify against [the] house of Jacob, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, the God of the hosts.
pieces: Listen, and be witnesses against Jacob's house, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, the God of Armies.

L.13: Hear, and bear witness against the house of Jacob, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, the God of hosts.

R.13: Listen, and be witnesses against the descendants of Jacob, \q says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, the God of Armies.

decisions.choice: hear and bear witness: spoken to the foreign witnesses of verse 9
decisions.reason: The commands are plural, and no new hearers are named, so they are most naturally addressed to the peoples called in verse 9 to look at Samaria. Now they are to bear witness against Israel. The verb means to testify against someone, or to warn them solemnly (Deuteronomy 8:19; 2 Kings 17:13).

decisions.choice: the house of Jacob: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Jacob is Israel's ancestor, and "the house of Jacob" is the nation descended from him, here the northern kingdom (compare 7:2, 5).

decisions.choice: the Lord GOD, the God of hosts: the fullest form of the title in Amos
decisions.reason: "Hosts" are armies, the armies of heaven that the LORD commands; the main note on the title is at Isaiah 1:9. Amos calls the LORD "the God of hosts" again in 4:13; 5:14-16, 27; 6:8, 14; 9:5. Here the title gathers "Lord", the divine name, and "God of hosts" together, to show who is bringing the charge.

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD, the God of hosts (L); declares the Lord GOD, the God of Armies (B); says the Lord GOD, the God of Armies (R)
decisions.reason: These are the settled wordings: "declares" (Literal, Balanced) and "says" (Readable) for the formula, "the Lord GOD" for the Lord with the divine name, and "the God of hosts" (Literal) or "the God of Armies" (Balanced, Readable) for the title. Where the title follows the divine name directly (4:13; 5:14-16), it is "the LORD God of hosts" and "the LORD God of Armies", as in the Psalms. Readable says "the descendants of Jacob" for "the house of Jacob" (m2).

records.source: כִּ֗י בְּי֛וֹם פָּקְדִ֥י פִשְׁעֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עָלָ֑יו וּפָֽקַדְתִּי֙ עַל־מִזְבְּח֣וֹת בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל וְנִגְדְּעוּ֙ קַרְנ֣וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וְנָפְל֖וּ לָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: For on [the] day I visit [the] transgressions of Israel on it, I will visit on [the] altars of Bethel, and will be cut off [the] horns of the altar and will fall to the ground.
pieces: On the day I punish Israel for its crimes, \q I will punish the altars of Bethel; \q the horns of the altar will be broken off \q and fall to the ground.

L.14: For on the day I punish the transgressions of Israel upon it, \q I will punish the altars of Bethel, \q and the altar's horns will be cut off \q and will fall to the ground.

R.14: On the day I punish Israel for its sins, \q I will also destroy the altars at Bethel. \q The horns on the corners of the altar will be chopped off \q and fall to the ground.

decisions.choice: I punish ... I will punish: the verb of verse 2 again, now aimed at Bethel
decisions.reason: The verb of verse 2 ("punish", often translated "visit") is used twice. The first clause names the day of judgment on Israel's crimes; the second says where it will strike first: the altars where Israel sought to make peace with God. This is the content of the testimony called for in verse 13.

decisions.choice: the altars of Bethel: the royal shrine of the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Jeroboam I set up a golden calf at Bethel and made it the main shrine of the northern kingdom (1 Kings 12:28-33); in Amos's day it was "the king's sanctuary" (7:13). The plural "altars" may mean the many altars there, or the shrine as a whole.

decisions.choice: the horns of the altar: the corner projections, where atonement was made and refuge sought
decisions.reason: An altar had a horn-shaped projection at each corner (Exodus 27:2). Blood was put on them to make atonement (Leviticus 4:7), and a fugitive could grasp them to claim protection (1 Kings 1:50-51; 2:28). With the horns cut off there is no atonement and no refuge.

decisions.choice: transgressions (L), crimes (B), sins (R); punish (L, B), destroy (R)
decisions.reason: The word for transgression follows Amos's settled wording; Balanced says "crimes", as in the refrain of 2:6. Readable says "destroy" for the second "punish", since it is the altars that are punished.

records.source: וְהִכֵּיתִ֥י בֵית־הַחֹ֖רֶף עַל־בֵּ֣ית הַקָּ֑יִץ וְאָבְד֞וּ בָּתֵּ֣י הַשֵּׁ֗ן וְסָפ֛וּ בָּתִּ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And I will strike [the] house of the winter along with [the] house of the summer, and will perish [the] houses of the ivory, and will come to an end great houses, declares Yahweh.
pieces: I will strike down the winter house together with the summer house; \q the houses of ivory will be destroyed, and the great houses will be swept away, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.15: And I will strike the winter house along with the summer house, \q and the ivory houses will perish, and great houses will come to an end, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.15: I will destroy the houses where the rich live in winter and their houses for summer. \q The houses decorated with ivory will be ruined, and the great houses will be gone, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the winter house and the summer house: the separate homes of the rich for each season
decisions.reason: Kings and the wealthy had one house for the cold, wet winter, perhaps in a warmer place, and another for the summer (Jeremiah 36:22 mentions the king's winter house). Owning two was a mark of great wealth.

decisions.choice: houses of ivory: houses decorated with carved ivory panels
decisions.reason: Ivory was carved into panels and inlaid in walls and furniture. Ahab built an "ivory house" in Samaria (1 Kings 22:39; compare Psalm 45:9), and many carved ivory pieces from this period have been found in the ruins of Samaria.

decisions.choice: great houses: the mansions of the rich
decisions.reason: The word can mean "great" or "many". Beside "houses of ivory", "great" fits best, but "many houses" is possible.

decisions.choice: the houses where the rich live in winter; decorated with ivory
decisions.reason: Readable says whose houses these are and what "houses of ivory" means (m1, m2).
